作為膜鳴樂器，鼓的音色主要由鼓面振動與鼓身共鳴決定。音域可隨鼓身尺寸與張力改變：: As a membranophone, a drum's timbre is decided mainly by the vibration of the head and the resonance of the shell. The range can change with the size of the shell and with the tension: the higher the tension, the higher the pitch and the lower the volume; the larger the diameter of the shell the lower the sound, and the greater the depth and thickness the louder; the speed and angle of the stroke also affect the volume. The thicker the head, or the more it is coated or fitted with a tone ring, the fewer the overtones and the drier the sound; a single-ply head has more overtones. Different shell shapes and single- or double-headed designs make the timbres clearly different: a bowl-shaped timpani can be tuned to a particular pitch, while a truncated-cone or goblet-shaped drum has a resonance of its own. Jazz drummers mostly choose drums that are high, resonant and quiet; rock drummers prefer drums that are loud, low and drier.

演奏鼓時，先將鼓穩置於地面、支架或腿上，使鼓面朝向演奏者；以手掌、指腹或鼓棒、鼓: To play a drum, first set it firmly on the floor, on a stand or on the legs, with the head facing the player; strike the head with the palm, the pads of the fingers, a drumstick or a beater, and a pedal and beater can also be used. A beginner can first practise with one hand, then add the other hand or brushes, keeping the wrist relaxed. With a set of drums or a kit, first learn where each drum and cymbal is, then strike them in turn to the rhythm pattern. Adjusting the tension of the head changes pitch and volume: higher tension gives a higher pitch and a lower volume.

鼓是打擊樂器中的膜鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sachs分類為211筒形鼓。構: The drum is the membranophone among percussion instruments, classed in Hornbostel–Sachs as 211, the cylindrical drums. At least one head or skin is stretched over the shell, usually with a resonating head below, and the sound is made by striking with the hand, a drumstick, a beater or a pedal and beater. A drum can be played alone, or two or more can be set up as a group, and with cymbals they make the modern drum kit. It appears in popular music, jazz, traditional religious rites, music therapy and military settings, and is played by drummers, by participants in ritual and by military personnel.
鼓的基本發聲體是張於鼓身開口的膜，來源提及鱷魚皮鼓面；現代鼓面另有雙層、白色塗層: The basic sounding body of a drum is the head stretched over the opening of the shell, and the source mentions crocodile skin for a head; modern heads may be double-ply, white-coated, with a silver-black dot in the centre or a tone ring at the edge, but the material is not stated. The shell may be of wood — the source mentions mahogany, maple and birch — and hollowed trunks, metal barrels and bronze Dong Son drums also occur. The other parts include the rim that holds the head, tension rods and lugs, and the metal snare that runs across the head; the beaters are wooden sticks and felt beaters, and the source also mentions brushes without giving their material.
鼓的聆聽場合涵蓋流行音樂、爵士樂與搖滾樂，常以鼓組搭配銅鈸，由鼓手以鼓棒、鼓刷或: Where you hear the drum covers pop, jazz and rock, usually a kit with cymbals, played with sticks, brushes or a foot pedal. In traditional cultures the drum serves religious rites, community communication and military signals: the African talking drum imitates the tones of speech, the karyenda drum of Burundi stood for royal power, and drums in Sri Lanka served as a means of state and community communication. Music therapy often uses hand drums, because they are tactile and easy to handle. In the orchestra and in modern ensembles, tuned drums such as the timpani can make up a particular line-up.
鼓的起源可追溯至新石器時代，中國有西元前5500至前2350年鱷魚皮鼓；西元前六: The origin of the drum can be traced to the Neolithic: China has crocodile-skin drums of 5500 to 2350 BC, and Mesopotamia had drums by 6000 BC. In the Bronze Age the Dong Son culture of northern Vietnam made bronze drums. Drums have long served for communication and as a sign of power: the African talking drum imitates the tones of speech, drums in Sri Lanka have a history of more than 2,500 years as a means of state and community communication, and the karyenda drum of Burundi stood for royal power. In war, Chinese armies used drums to raise morale, and Swiss mercenaries used early side drums; in modern pop and jazz the word drum usually means the kit of drums and cymbals.
